subtopics.title: Digital Platforms and Online Gaming
subtopics.summary: A US jury found Meta Platforms and YouTube liable for addictive platform design, shifting attention from content to design. India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prohibits online money gaming, and the PROG Rules 2026 take effect from 1 May 2026. UPI completed 10 years in 2026 as a leading real-time payment system.

subtopics.title: International Relations

India and South Korea elevated ties to a Futuristic Partnership under a Joint Strategic Vision during President Lee Jae-myung's visit.

subtopics.title: Polity, Governance and Schemes
subtopics.summary: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that Scheduled Caste status is limited to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists, so conversion to another religion leads to loss of SC status. Parliament passed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, naming Amaravati as the sole capital. Several government schemes were also extended or expanded, including the PM Internship Scheme and PMGSY-III.

subtopics.title: Historical Events and Personalities
subtopics.summary: The 1526 Battle of Panipat between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi marked the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India. The section also covers the Sikh Gurus, the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, Shaheed Diwas, and the reformers Jyotirao Phule and B. R. Ambedkar. Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi on the orders of Aurangzeb.

quizzes.passage: Polity and governance decisions often turn on precise legal definitions. The Scheduled Caste list is set through an order issued in 1950, and recent court rulings have examined how a person's religion affects membership of that list. Membership is not the only area where Parliament is active. It has passed legislation that deals with the legal position of a state capital, after an arrangement in which two states shared a common capital came to an end. The government has also extended and expanded several welfare schemes. The PM Internship Scheme offers internships to young people and is run by a central ministry, while PMGSY-III is a road programme for rural habitations that has been extended for a further period. Under the Namo Drone Didi Yojana, drones are provided to rural women for agricultural work such as crop spraying and fertiliser application. Karnataka has been named a top performer under this scheme. Each scheme has a defined objective, such as connecting rural areas with the mainstream economy or empowering women in farming. Many of these programmes depend on state-level agencies to carry out the work on the ground, and their funding is shared between the Centre and the states in fixed proportions.

quizzes.passage: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana is a centrally sponsored scheme whose objective is to provide all-weather road connectivity to rural habitations. Its third phase has been extended by the Union Cabinet for a further period, and funding is shared between the Centre and the states in fixed proportions, with the North-Eastern and Himalayan states receiving a higher central share. Implementation takes place through state-level agencies, supported by a central agency. The Namo Drone Didi Yojana aims to empower rural women by providing agricultural drones for crop spraying and precision farming. Drones are distributed to self-help groups, and the cost is met partly through a subsidy and partly through loans. The nodal authority for the drone scheme is the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The remaining share of the cost comes through loans under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, and Karnataka has been named a top performer under the drone scheme. The PM Internship Scheme is open to candidates within a set age range, and it offers placements at large companies. It has been expanded to include final-year students. Insurance cover under two national life and accident schemes is also part of the internship package. Eligibility rules, including family income and government employment, decide who can apply.

quizzes.passage: India's position in global economic rankings is measured using nominal GDP in US dollar terms. The figure depends on domestic output in rupees and on the exchange rate against the dollar, so a weaker rupee lowers the dollar value of GDP. A revision of GDP data with a new base year also changes the figures. Special Additional Excise Duty, or SAED, is a levy on petroleum products that the government adjusts when global crude prices move. It works as a windfall tax in times of price surges, and unlike the GST, its revenue is kept by the Centre. Climate policy is another area of activity. Countries submit self-defined climate action plans under the Paris framework, and these plans are reported regularly. Synthetic gases used in cooling and foam industries are being phased down under an international amendment to the Montreal Protocol. Air conditioners and refrigerators are among the uses of these synthetic gases. Host nations for the UN climate conference are chosen through regional rotation. The rules also require a formal proposal to the UNFCCC Secretariat before a country can be chosen. If no host emerges, the venue shifts to Bonn, the seat of the UNFCCC. Rankings also influence investor sentiment and global confidence.

quizzes.passage: Economic rankings depend on how an economy's output is valued. Countries are compared by nominal GDP in dollar terms, so the figures move with the exchange rate. When the domestic currency weakens, the same output is worth fewer dollars. The government also revises GDP series when a new base year is introduced, and such revisions change the level of output reported for earlier years. Separately, the government uses a special duty on petroleum products that is revised regularly, and its revenue is not divided with states the way GST revenue is. States therefore receive no share of that revenue, which goes to the Central Government. On the climate side, countries prepare national climate plans under the Paris framework, which are reported and updated over time. Such plans are not legally binding, but reporting is mandatory. The host of the annual UN climate conference is chosen through a rotation among regional groups. Finally, the use of synthetic gases in cooling and foam is being restricted under an international agreement aimed at reducing global warming. The ranking figures are therefore sensitive to currency movements and to statistical revisions. A fall in rank does not by itself signal an economic slowdown. India remains among the fastest-growing major economies.

quizzes.passage: Several episodes in the history of India show how political events shaped public life. A battle near Panipat, in present-day Haryana, is remembered as a turning point in medieval history, and its military methods drew on techniques from West Asia. The Sikh community was shaped by a line of Gurus who built towns and developed their own institutions. Their teachings and practices were preserved and passed on over generations. In 1919, a gathering in Amritsar on a spring festival day was fired on by colonial troops, and the incident caused deep anger across the country. Protests that followed were linked to laws that allowed detention without trial, and to the arrest of local leaders. An official inquiry criticised the commander but imposed no severe punishment. The gathering had come together for a Baisakhi celebration and to protest against recent arrests. The massacre is still remembered as one of the most brutal episodes of colonial rule. Reformers of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries also worked for social change. One campaigned for the education of women and the rights of lower castes, and another helped draft the Constitution of India. The Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920, led by Gandhi, marked a shift in the freedom struggle. Their work is commemorated through national observances.

quizzes.passage: Historical episodes in India are often remembered through anniversaries and observances. Sikh history is shaped by a line of Gurus whose teachings and institutions developed the community over more than two centuries. The first of them is regarded as the founder of the faith, while later Gurus built towns, established shared meals for visitors and oversaw the creation of sacred texts. A military campaign in the early sixteenth century is also part of this history. The invader who fought near Panipat had earlier held territory in Central Asia, and the battle is remembered as a turning point in medieval India. The battle is also linked to the later Mughal empire in India, and Panipat is in present-day Haryana. Reformers of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries also left a lasting mark. One opened a school for girls in Pune with his wife, while another campaigned against caste discrimination and later helped draft the Constitution. A young revolutionary generation is remembered too, including men who were executed in a Lahore jail in the 1930s and are honoured every year. Such figures are honoured on national days, with tributes from national leaders. The events and figures in this section show how faith, war and social reform shaped modern India.
